comparison.objective: Seat and level a surface-roughness drive with a thumbscrew, then run its traverse; the candidate adjusts and locks a gripper opening stop before cycling it.
comparison.physical_skill: Precision seating on a shaft and anvil followed by single-screw leveling versus simultaneous driver counterholding and thin-jam-nut tightening on one coupled adjustment.
comparison.success_condition: Requires seated geometry, horizontal level, completed 4.790 mm traverse, and clear hands; candidate requires a retained 90° stop, locked nuts, and three repeatable cycles.
comparison.reason: This is the closest record because both adjust a mechanism and function-test it, but it lacks the candidate's defining ability: locking an adjustable screw without disturbing its setting.
